## Historical audit — S0319

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H02/development/commons_192968130/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below are JSONL lines in this file; observations are unsplit.

**Goal versus evidence:** The requested goal was to reconstruct a photograph as separate, editable SceneAct/Blender meshes with matching framing and materials. The student interpreted the scene as a modern kitchen; that interpretation and its image-anchor estimates are not independent verification of the photograph (line 1, `model_request`; line 3, H `model_response`).

| Stage | Observed evidence |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H emitted multiple named assets: room surfaces, slatted wall, door and handle, sideboard, counter, hob, sink and upper cabinets. Child parts were grouped with `include`; no physical attachment or support validation is reported. Colors and geometric seams/veins approximate materials, rather than demonstrating texture fidelity. The sink is layered flat boxes, not a cut basin. A camera, world and three area lights were specified (lines 3–4). No articulated-person pose is involved; object placement and camera pose remain estimates. |
| First feedback and revision | Build and render completed, and step 1 was selected (lines 6, 8–10). The next request actually supplied the reference, rendered image and comparison instructions (line 11). H reported a too-small door/back wall, excess floor and pale cabinets; these are student observations, not independently visible to this audit. It moved the camera forward, extended the wall, repositioned the hob and sink, and darkened materials and lighting (lines 13–14). |
| Second feedback and revision | Step 2 built and rendered successfully (lines 16, 18–20); the reference and render were supplied again (line 21). H reported a missing hob, light peach cabinets and displaced anchors; it moved the hob, shifted the sideboard, adjusted camera target, raised slats, widened/lowered cabinets and reduced lights. These changes were executed, not merely proposed (lines 23–24). |
| Outcome | Step 3 build and render returned success and step 3 was selected (lines 26, 28–30). This is **technical execution success**, not demonstrated reconstruction correctness. No final image review, `DONE`, independent geometric check, or formal quality score appears in the supplied record. |

**Input and autonomy:** The visible instructional feedback came from the runner’s user messages, not a separately identified teacher. H’s subsequent comparison comments and edits show use of that feedback, but there is no evidence of a separate teacher diagnosis or teacher-authored update. The recorded Codex sessions report no tool calls; exploration consisted of the three generated scene programs and runner renders, not observed external search or interactive inspection (lines 2, 12, 22).

**Transferable lesson and uncertainty:** Comparing foreground and background anchors can motivate separate camera and local-asset changes, while brightness may depend on both lighting and material. Here those diagnoses and predicted improvements remain hypotheses: neither reference nor render pixels are included in the audit text. In particular, final object visibility, part connections, pose/framing, textures, lighting and whether the hob correction worked cannot be independently established. The second program’s estimate of 46 slat-wall parts also conflicts with its 64-slat loop (line 13), illustrating that an estimate is not a count validation.
